summary: The patch tries to undo newline translation after the fact via blind string replacement instead of preventing the translation at the source (open the capture buffer with newline=""). This unconditionally rewrites every '\n' to '\r\n', corrupting genuine newlines in all captured output — a broad regression and a fragile, incorrect approach.

issues.description: Wrong abstraction: once the text buffer has translated line endings, original '\r' vs '\n' vs '\r\n' are indistinguishable, so a post-hoc replace cannot faithfully reconstruct input. Correct fix is to disable universal-newline translation on the capture file (newline=""), not reverse-engineer it.

Heuristic is shaped to make the '\r'-ending reproducer pass rather than to solve newline handling generally; behavior on mixed/interleaved '\r' and '\n' is unspecified and likely wrong.
Single-quoted string literals inconsistent with pytest's black/double-quote convention.
